comments.text:
I've got a 11th gen w-1370 with uhd p750 and just recently bought an a310. The igpu does one or two parallell 4k hdr hevc to 4k hdr hevc transcodes with Plex. But with the a310 I've managed to transcode 8(!) 4k streams simultaneously.. Of course this was just benchmarking to see how many streams I could do, it's not a real life scenario, and having 8 running instances the streams buffer maybe 10 seconds before playing if I jump to a place in the time bar that's not cached yet. But the card does manage to play them all without hiccups and the igpu is nowhere near that performance.

Some details: Plex is in a docker container on an ubuntu server lxc in Proxmox. Resizable bar is enabled in the bios and huc/guc is enabled in the Linux kernel. I've got 128 gb of ram and a 16 gb RAM disk that plex is transcoding to. My a310 is connected to a pcie 3.0 x1 pcie slot that might hamper it but I currently have no way of trying it out on a full bandwidth slot so there's no telling.

What I've seen online, this is not doable with Plex server on a windows machine. There the a310 seems to handle mabe  2-3 4k hevc transcodes.

When it comes to Jellyfin, I'm not as well-versed. When I tested it, I was able to transcode "only" 7 streams, but that might just be because my settings aren't optimal. Also, considering I'm on only one pcie 3.0 lane this can also factor in if Jellyfin handles things differently than plex.

@samiraperi467  False. With x16 physical slots, they are arranged in a 25/75 power configuration for regular and high-power devices. 
So, for example an 8x RAID card in a x16 physical slot can operate in 25-watt mode while a graphics card operates in 75-watt (high-power) mode.
1x slots are only configured for 12/25 watt modes. The same RAID card will signal that it needs 25 watts and run just fine. A NIC would request 12-watt mode.
This card would signal for high-power mode and the chipset would reply with 25 watts. 
You'd have all manner of weirdness trying to run this card, which requires 50 watts, in many circumstances.

comments.text:
Yes, it is fully supported by Tdarr. I'd recommend using the Arc-specific Docker images if using Docker.
If not using Docker, just set the node properties to QSV, enable "GPU can perform CPU Tasks", and you're off to the races.
I would not recommend a P400 unless you already own it. 
If you're buying something new/used, and you're doing enough transcoding to justify a card, then the Arc is the better choice.
